Let’s dive into Chapter 9: Trust Across Cultures and Differences.
In today’s world, where we’re more connected and diverse than ever, trust isn’t just about understanding the people who are most like us. It’s about reaching across backgrounds, values, and even the way we talk to each other. What builds trust for you might not work the same way for someone from a completely different culture. And that’s why learning how to bridge those gaps is so important.
Think about it—cultural differences can really shape how trust is given and received. Some cultures appreciate directness and being upfront, while others lean towards harmony and might prefer a more indirect approach. You might find that in one place, trust grows through personal relationships, but somewhere else, it’s all about your credentials or how well you perform.
So, how do you build trust across these differences? Here are a few things to keep in mind.
First, take the time to learn about and respect different norms and expectations. Be genuinely curious—ask questions instead of making assumptions. It’s amazing how much you can learn just by being open and willing to listen.
Next, try to adapt your communication style to fit your audience. Maybe you need to be a little more direct, or perhaps it’s better to ease into things. And look for common ground—shared goals, values, even little experiences you can connect over.
Let’s say you’re leading a multinational team, and you notice some team members are hesitant to speak up during meetings. Instead of pushing everyone to talk in a big group, what if you created smaller discussion groups or even invited people to share their thoughts in writing? That small change can make a huge difference, giving everyone a safer space to contribute.
And it’s not just about culture. Trust is also shaped by age, gender, and background. We all have unconscious biases, but being aware of them—and making space for different perspectives—can really strengthen trust and help your team get better results.
At the end of the day, trust across differences comes down to empathy and respect. When people feel truly seen and valued for who they are, trust just grows naturally.
